extracted.intended_audience: students and merchants learning classical arithmetic and proportions
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and procedures for working with continued proportional parts: multiplying proportional sequences, extracting squares/cubes/fourths, scaling money/capital and combining alloys/percentages; presented in an early-modern Italian arithmetic/textbook style with worked examples. Useful for solving merchant arithmetic and proportion problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiplication of continued proportional parts
rubrics_metrics.description: Original phrasing: 'Quanno tre parti continue proportionali che multiplicata la pÿima via la feconda fanno quanto el quadrato de la ter^a' (rules relating products of terms of a continued proportion to squares/cubes of other terms).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains that products of specific terms in a continued proportional sequence yield squares or cubes of other terms; shows how to multiply the first and second to relate to the square of the third, how other multiplicative combinations give cubes or higher powers. Numerous numeric illustrations (e.g. examples producing 916, 2304, 4096) show reduction to squares/cubes and comparison of results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finding a missing proportional (third/fourth) by multiplication and division
rubrics_metrics.description: Original phrasing scattered: 'trouare la ter^a per via ... multiplicata ... fare vna altra positione' — methods to determine a missing proportional by arranging multiplications/divisions among the known terms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedure: form appropriate products of known terms (often multiply extremes or means), then divide by one of the given terms to obtain the missing proportional; uses binomial decomposition and successive division to isolate the unknown. Examples include finding third and fourth proportionals via multiplying chosen terms and dividing by given ones.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scaling capital and gains over time (proportional scaling of money/interest)
rubrics_metrics.description: Pervasive merchant-arithmetic rule: multiply capital by growth-factors per period to compute future value; conversely divide future value by period factors to recover capital. (Text: many passages on 'capitale e guadagno', 'multiplicare via il capitale o del secondo giorno').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains treating capital and daily gains as proportional factors: to get the aggregate after multiple periods multiply sequentially by each period's factor; to revert find successive quotients. Worked examples convert days' gains to multiples of capital and show how to compute resulting totals and per-period shares.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combining alloys/mixtures by weighted proportions
rubrics_metrics.description: Original wording examples: 'la lega de le fo.te ... farne un bolzone ... la lega de i p[c]arti' — rules for mixing different metals or qualities (leghe) and computing resulting composition/value via proportions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prescribes forming weighted sums: multiply each component's amount by its purity/value, add the contributions, then divide by total weight to find the mixture's average purity/value. Shows creating a combined 'bolzone' and then decomposing to see which original proportions yield a desired alloy. Numeric examples illustrate multiple-component mixtures and conversion to denomination values.

rubrics_metrics.name: Using binomial/nonuple (multiple) multiplications to simplify repeated proportional operations
rubrics_metrics.description: Text repeatedly uses language about multiplying by 2, 3, 4, 8, 12, etc., and 'binomio', 'nonupla' to reduce long chains of proportion multiplications. (e.g., 'moltiplicato per 3 fa quanto il quadrato od ter^o', 'moltiplicato per 8 fa ...')
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When many successive proportional multiplications are required, the text recommends grouping via binomial or higher-fold multipliers (double, triple, quadruple, octuple, nonuple) to shorten work: replace repeated single multiplications by a single multiplication by the appropriate composite factor, then reduce by extracting powers or dividing by appropriate factors. Examples show collapsing long sequences into manageable multiplications (e.g., 8×, 9×, 12× multipliers) and tracking resulting powers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduction of proportional sequences by extracting universal roots (squares, cubes, fourths)
rubrics_metrics.description: Original sense: transform long multiplicative results by recognizing they are perfect squares/cubes/fourths and extracting roots to simplify and compare ('ridurrete al primo ... estrarre la radice universale').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After performing multiplicative operations which yield large numbers, identify when results are perfect powers so you can extract square/cube/fourth roots to return to original-scale terms; the text gives tables and worked numbers demonstrating when products correspond to these powers and how to reduce them for comparison or further operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparing proportional terms via their squares/cubes to establish equality or ratios
rubrics_metrics.description: Instructional rule: compare the surfaces (squares) or volumes (cubes) derived from proportional terms to deduce proportional relationships among the original terms ('quadra la prima fa ... quadra la seconda fa ... quelli faranno eguale a ...')
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To test whether proportional relations hold, square or cube the candidate terms (or take other powers) and compare the resulting numbers; equalities among these powers imply proportionalities among the base terms. The text includes many numeric verifications (e.g., 64, 256, 4096) showing equality/non-equality through powers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aggregating multiple proportional multiplications to compute totals and mixtures
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on summing the results of several proportional multiplications to obtain a combined total or mixture value (e.g., summing contributions from multiple multiplicative operations to get final 'fuma' or 'bolzone').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perform each proportional multiplication for individual components, then add component results to obtain the aggregated quantity or monetary value. The method is illustrated with multi-component examples where each component has been multiplied by its factor and the totals compared or equated to target values.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finding remainders and quotients by successive division after multiplicative steps
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures: after multiplying chosen terms, divide successively by binomial factors or given divisors to obtain quotients (remainders are tracked and sometimes factorized further to continue the process).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The method prescribes repeated division of large products by known divisors to isolate terms or residuals; when remainders appear, continue factoring the remainder by further division or by recognizing power-structure (e.g., dividing 47949... by 22, 52, etc., as in the examples). This yields stepwise extraction of the desired proportional term.

rubrics_metrics.name: Algorithmic step-by-step process for operations on series of proportional numbers
rubrics_metrics.description: Throughout the text there is an implied algorithm: select which terms to multiply (extremes/means), multiply them (possibly grouping multipliers), divide by chosen known terms, reduce by extracting powers, and aggregate results as needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text models a stepwise approach: (1) decide the positions (which terms to multiply), (2) perform grouped multiplications using binomial/nonuple shortcuts, (3) divide by designated terms to isolate unknowns, (4) reduce by extracting roots/powers when products are perfect powers, (5) sum component results for totals, and (6) check by recomputing squares/cubes. Numerous worked numeric examples demonstrate each step.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical numeric heuristics and example-driven verification
rubrics_metrics.description: The book repeatedly endorses checking work by recomputing via different routes (e.g., multiplying in alternative orders, squaring/cubing results, or re-aggregating components) as a method of verification ('guarda le multiplicationi che tu ha gia' giovnere ... )'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use multiple computational routes to verify results: perform the multiplicative chain in a different grouped order, compare powers (squares/cubes), and re-sum components. The text's many explicit numeric examples (capital/interest calculations, alloy mixtures, long-chain proportional multiplications) serve both as heuristics and verifications.
